SMTO-EXE-0030 — There was no command to run

GUID: cef5721c-1c0d-4172-8bb7-e7bba0d17e5f
Slug: terminal-command-required
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • SMTO was asked to run a command, but the command text was empty. Nothing was run and nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you typed or edited a command yourself, make sure the command box isn't empty or just spaces before you run it. SMTO refuses a blank command because there is nothing to run.
  2. If this happened while SMTO was working on a task, tell it in the conversation exactly what you want done, for example the command or the result you need. Clear instructions give SMTO the command text it was missing.
  3. Ask SMTO to continue the task. Nothing ran the first time, so continuing is safe once the command is filled in.

What success looks like

  • The step shows the command it ran and that command's output.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the conversation name, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep resending a blank command; it will be refused the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gateway exec, job, streaming or terminal request carried empty or whitespace-only command text and was rejected before any process was started.

What this means

  • An execution, job or terminal request supplied no usable command text after its applicable empty/whitespace validation. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • An execution, job or terminal request supplied no usable command text after its applicable empty/whitespace validation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the submitted command field and request kind; an existing terminal session does not supply missing command text automatically.

How to fix it

  • Check the command field of the rejected request (gateway_core.app exec routes, GatewayService.job/exec/exec_stream/terminal_exec_stream/terminal_exec_detach, TerminalSession.start_detached_command). Supply the intended non-empty command through the same execution action; the request is rejected before process creation.
  • Supply the intended command text through the existing execution action.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended nonempty command passes admission under its normal target and policy checks.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
